title: Introducing Category Theory (2nd edition)
byline: Peter Smith · Logic Matters, version 2.1, 2025 (free PDF)
note: Short “Challenges!” and “Responses” subsections are not broken out; the interlude and bibliography are not covered. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A slow-paced, carefully motivated introduction to category theory for philosophers, logicians and mathematics students, by a logician known for teaching texts. Smith starts from categories of groups and questions about sets, classes and size, then builds the elementary theory: arrows and their kinds, initial and terminal objects, products and coproducts (first “pre-categorially”), internal groups, equalizers, exponentials and cartesian closed categories, limits and colimits, pullbacks and the existence of limits, subobjects and subobject classifiers. The middle part covers functors, comma categories, hom-functors, natural transformations, equivalence of categories, functor categories, Yoneda and representables, Galois connections and adjunctions. The final part introduces elementary toposes: power objects, natural numbers objects, internal logic, subobject lattices, complements, well-pointedness and ETCS.
